name: NCCL is not supported with MIG, so a MIG slice cannot participate in a tensor-parallel group - MIG and TP are mutually exclusive as shipped
symptom: Planning error rather than a runtime crash: an operator who partitions an H100 into MIG instances and then tries to run TP=2 inside them gets NCCL unsupported-with-MIG rather than a working deployment. The NVIDIA MIG User Guide lists it flatly under Application Considerations: 'NCCL is currently not supported with MIG.' The request to lift this has been open on NCCL since at least 2025 (NCCL #1716), whose stated motivation is exactly this use case: 'It'd much cheaper to rent 1x A100 or H100 split it 4 way and do a 4-way gpu testing on CI, than paying for 4 gpus.'
root_cause: MIG instances are exposed as separate CUDA devices with their own GPU and Compute Instance scoping, and the vendor documents a matching set of restrictions that make collective communication across them non-functional: with driver R570 only P2P between MIG instances on the same GPU is supported - 'P2P between MIG instances on different GPUs, or between MIG instances to non-MIG mode GPU devices are not supported'; 'CUDA IPC across GPU instances is not supported. CUDA IPC across Compute instances is supported.' A collective library needs P2P or IPC across the group, so NCCL support was never enabled on MIG.
workaround: Do not combine MIG with TP or EP. Either partition the GPU with MIG and run one engine per slice at TP=1 (the supported multi-tenant pattern), or leave MIG off and shard with TP across physical GPUs. If the need is many-GPU CI, MIG alone is the answer and the TP axis has to be dropped. Note CUDA IPC works across Compute instances within one GPU Instance, so MPS-style co-location of several ranks inside one GI is the closest supported approximation.
notes: The same section of the guide blocks CUDA IPC across GPU Instances but permits it across Compute Instances - that asymmetry is the mechanism behind mgpu-mps-max-clients-scale-down-on-mig. Do not read 'MIG supports up to seven instances' as 'MIG gives you a 7-GPU TP group'.
